newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Aussie makes last gap bounce after new low.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Aussie makes last gap bounce after new low.

text.p: *AUD extended downtrend for third offshore session to all but fulfill $0.7680 bear target as European and US banks sold
*Asian bids emerged there and forced short covering bounce to $0.7740 but break of $0.7720 had confirmed bearish trend
*Recapture of $0.7785 needed to forestall further decline, otherwise AUD risks return to $0.7600/30 band from February
By 8.15 am (2215 GMT) the local dollar had clawed its way back to US$0.7740/45 from that US$0.7695 low and was only a shade off Wednesday's late US$0.7745/50.

Analysts said the currency needed to recapture US$0.7785 today to forestall another tilt at the downside, while a breach of US$0.7680 would open the way for a return to the US$.7600/30 band which provided support in February and perhaps even the US$0.7550 from February 12.
On the crosses the currency had bounced to 97.40/50 yen from a 96.65 low and was again only a touch off Wednesday's late 97.55/65, partly mirroring price action in the U.S. dollar.
The U.S. unit was curbed by caution over possible central bank intervention, but underpinned by a strong 0.9 percent rise in U.S. industrial production and tightening utilisation.

The figures also had implications for the local dollar since they increased the chance of the Federal Reserve hiking rates again at its May 20 meeting, so further narrowing the A$'s already slender yield premium.

However, the fact the world's biggest economy was running so fast boded well for a pick up in growth in Japan and Europe and a corresponding lift in the demand for, and price of, commodities -- Australia's biggest export.
That was a long term prospect, however, and in the meantime the erosion of the A$'s yield advantage over the US$ was set to dominate market sentiment.
Dealers noted domestic rates on six month money had joined the one-year by slipping below U.S. levels overnight and six-month A$ forwards had moved to a slight premium, a very rare event indeed.

There was some upbeat news for the dollar with confirmation of market rumours that Victoria was close to selling a power station to a U.S.-led consortium for around A$4.5 billion, implying a need to buy A$. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
